recipe.goal: Gravitational lens modelling and pixelised source-plane reconstruction of continuum and line cubes
recipe.method: Simultaneously fit Band 4 continuum visibilities (time-averaged to 20s) and Band 7 visibilities in the uv-plane using an elliptical power-law mass profile and linear inversion on a randomized Voronoi source grid; reconstruct channel slices by averaging 50 random Voronoi pixelisations onto a 100x100 grid.
key_parameters: 0.8 x 0.8 arcsec source plane with 400 Voronoi pixels, 7 randomisations per likelihood evaluation, 50 randomisations averaged onto 100 x 100 square pixels for final reconstruction, 20s visibility time-averaging in Band 4
assumptions: Elliptical power-law volume mass density profile for the foreground lens with zero external shear

recipe.goal: Far-IR SED fitting to derive dust mass, FIR luminosity, and star formation rate
recipe.method: Fit rest-frame continuum photometry with an optically thick single-temperature modified black-body SED and an optically thin two-temperature modified black-body SED, integrate from 8 to 1000 um for LFIR, and convert to SFR.
key_parameters: 4 degrees of freedom for optically thin two-component SED; 3 degrees of freedom for optically thick single-component SED; integration range 8-1000 um
assumptions: Fixed emissivity index beta = 2.0; dust mass absorption coefficient kappa_168um = 1.7 m^2 kg^-1; Kennicutt & Evans (2012) SFR conversion with Kroupa (2003) IMF

recipe.goal: Measure spatial variation of ISM excitation temperature and molecular mass fraction from [CI] lines
recipe.method: Divide reconstructed [CI](2-1) and [CI](1-0) source images into a stack of five east-west slices, compute line luminosity ratio R = L'(2-1)/L'(1-0), and convert to excitation temperature and molecular mass fraction per slice.
key_parameters: 5 slices running east-west, each 0.2 arcsec long and 0.08 arcsec wide
assumptions: Optically thin [CI] lines and local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE)

recipe.goal: Estimate total molecular ISM mass using four tracers and five methods
recipe.method: Calculate de-magnified luminosities of CO(1-0), [CI](1-0), [CII] 158um, and rest-frame 850um dust continuum (extrapolated from 3290um), and apply Galactic-calibrated conversion factors individually and via a combined CO/[CI]/dust method.
key_parameters: Magnification factors: mu = 5.5 for CO(1-0) and 3290um dust, mu = 5.6 for [CI](1-0), mu = 5.9 for [CII]
assumptions: alpha_CO = 3.0 +/- 0.5 M_sun (K km s^-1 pc^2)^-1 with 1.36 helium factor and mean GDR = 135; alpha_[CI] = 18.8 M_sun (K km s^-1 pc^2)^-1; alpha_CII = 30 M_sun/L_sun; alpha_850um = 6.7 +/- 1.7 x 10^19 ergs s^-1 Hz^-1 M_sun^-1 with T_d = 25 K and beta = 1.8

recipe.goal: Lens light subtraction in Spitzer IRAC and multi-wavelength SED fitting for stellar mass
recipe.method: Fit foreground lens surface brightness in Ks-band using GALFIT, construct and subtract model IRAC 3.6 and 4.5 um lens profiles, extract residual source flux in an annulus, and fit multi-wavelength photometry with MAGPHYS v2.
key_parameters: De-magnification factor mu = 5.8; IMF scaling factor = 1.41
assumptions: Near-IR Ks-band morphology traces mid-IR lens light; Chabrier (2003) IMF in MAGPHYS scaled by 1.41 to Kroupa (2003) IMF

recipe.goal: 3D kinematic tilted-ring modelling of reconstructed CO(7-6) and H2O cubes and dynamical mass estimation
recipe.method: Identify 3D source mask using 3DBarolo SEARCH (DUCHAMP), extract initial parameters from CASA moment maps and 2D Gaussian fits, fit tilted-ring models using 3DFIT with both local and azimuthal normalizations, and repeat after masking/subtracting the northern region with CASA immath to test a two-galaxy scenario.
key_parameters: SEARCH primary SNR threshold = 3.5 sigma, secondary threshold = 2.0 sigma; minimum ring width = 0.4 x FWHM of minor axis of restoring beam; maximum model radius = 0.8 x FWHM of major axis of 2D Gaussian fit to moment-0; disk scale height z_o = 0.01 arcsec; both local and azimuthal flux normalizations
assumptions: Thin rotating disk with circular orbits

recipe.goal: Chemical evolution modelling and dynamical stability/timescale analysis
recipe.method: Run chemical evolution models (conSF and 200 Myr SB) for Salpeter, Chabrier, and top-heavy IMFs to track GDR, metallicity, gas mass, and stellar mass; compute escape velocity, clump inspiral timescale, Toomre Q-parameter, and gas depletion time.
key_parameters: z_f = 4.8 (Salpeter), 5.5 (Chabrier), 7 (top-heavy); SB burst duration = 200 Myr observed at 40%; grain growth parameter = 700 to 15,000; effective radius = 1.4 kpc; v_c / sigma_0 = 10
assumptions: Milky Way GDR = 160 (with beta = 1.8, T_d = 25 K, kappa_850 = 0.077 m^2 kg^-1, kappa_ISM = 4.8 x 10^-4 m^2 kg^-1, equal HI and H2 plus Helium); zero dark matter contribution; M_gas / M_tot = 0.5 for Toomre Q

score_reason: Raw ALMA data, CASA versions, calibration script provenance, imaging pixel scale/weighting, best-fit lens model parameters, and 3DBarolo settings are clearly specified, and key intermediate and final numbers are tabulated. However, the custom visibility-plane Voronoi lens reconstruction code and chemical evolution code are not publicly released, and the appendices detailing MAGPHYS and chemical evolution parameters are absent.
rediscovery_reason: All three ALMA datasets are public in the archive, the observed lensed line and continuum fluxes and lens model parameters are explicitly reported as benchmarks, and standard tools (CASA, 3DBarolo) or open-source lens modelling alternatives (e.g. PyAutoLens) can be used to reproduce the source reconstructions, temperature gradient, kinematic fits, and ISM/dynamical masses.
